placet.title: Placet Group — Mobile Application
placet.description: A financial app for Placet Group, designed from scratch: a credit line, loans and a physical card in one place, built around clear financial states.
placet.listDescription: A financial app built from zero: credit line, loans and a physical card in one calm, readable interface.
placet.challenge: Placet’s customers found it inconvenient to take out and manage credit. There was no single, clear place to see a credit line, a loan or a card, and to act on them right away.
placet.solution:
Together with a member of Placet’s management, I led the art direction and designed the app from scratch, including its visual language.
The main decisions:
• Sign-in with Smart-ID, Mobile-ID or Face ID, so access is quick and trusted from the first tap.
• A dashboard that opens on what matters: available amount, next payment and two primary actions.
• Every product state is named plainly (in processing, active, overdue) with the next action right below it.
• The physical card journey is a simple timeline: ordered, shipped, expected, activated.
• Card controls are one tap away: contactless and online payments, PIN, transaction history.
• One system in dark and light themes.
placet.result: The app has not launched yet, so there are no usage results to report. What is finished is the full design: sign-in, dashboard, product states, card journey and card controls, in dark and light themes.

impact.label: Built from scratch
impact.description: Product structure, interface and visual language designed as one system.

impact.label: Themes
impact.description: Dark and light, from one design system.

screen1.title: Authentication & Face ID onboarding
screen1.description: Smart-ID and Mobile-ID sign-in behind a short welcome, followed by an optional Face ID step. Secure, but never more than a couple of taps.

screen2.title: Dashboard — credit line at a glance
screen2.description: Available amount, a repayment progress bar, the next payment date and amount, and two primary actions. The credit line and loans share one pattern, followed by a readable transaction feed.

screen3.title: Financial states — processing, active and overdue
screen3.description: Each product shows its state in plain words (in processing, active, overdue) with the actions that make sense in that state. Overdue debt is flagged at the top of the card, impossible to miss.

screen4.title: Card ordering and delivery timeline
screen4.description: Ordering a card and following it home: an offer, then a three-step timeline (ordered, shipped, expected), ending in an activation button once the card arrives.

screen5.title: Black Card controls and safety tools
screen5.description: Card controls in one place: contactless and online payment switches, transaction history, temporary suspension, PIN reminder and change. Activation takes a three-digit CVV on a native keypad.

screen6.title: Visual system — dark & light explorations
screen6.description: One visual language in dark and light themes: orange as the single accent, the honeycomb texture from the Placet brand, and the same components on every screen.

paskolos.title: Paskolos.lt — Credit Line
paskolos.description: Credit line product design with emphasis on transparency of terms and informed decision-making.
paskolos.listDescription: Credit line product design focused on transparent terms, limit management, and confident user decision-making.
paskolos.challenge:
At the product entry point, users struggled to quickly understand the difference between a credit line and a consumer loan, as well as determine which option suited their needs.
Fragmented offers and conditions turned the selection process into guesswork, reducing trust before the application even began.
paskolos.solution:
I separated the two products at both structural and scenario levels, creating clear entry points for the credit line and consumer loan.
Key decisions included:
• dedicated hero sections with clear offers for each product,
• visual and textual explanation of product differences,
• a simplified three-step flow for consumer loan applications,
• using the calculator and limit selection as the primary entry point for the credit line.
paskolos.result: Separate landing pages for the credit line and the consumer loan, a limit selector, a three-step application path and recommended products, designed for desktop and mobile.

placetSelfservice.title: Placet Group — Unified Self-Service
placetSelfservice.description: Unified self-service platform for multiple brands: loans, cards, documents, support.
placetSelfservice.listDescription: Unified self-service platform enabling users to manage loans, cards, and documents in one account across multiple brands.
placetSelfservice.challenge:
Users managed different financial products — loans, credit line, cards, and documents — through fragmented interfaces and scenarios.
The lack of a unified environment increased cognitive load, complicated navigation, and made it harder to understand the overall financial picture.
placetSelfservice.solution:
I designed a unified self-service platform that brings all user products and actions into a single, coherent interface.
Key decisions included:
• a unified overview of all financial products and states,
• consistent navigation across scenarios,
• reusable UX patterns for actions and statuses,
• a scalable structure for future products and features.
placetSelfservice.result: A single self-service environment for loans, credit lines and cards: application flows, a credit line dashboard, card management and card delivery, designed for desktop and mobile.
